sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption considers how universities can manage corruption risks arising from their international student businesses.
sentences.support: the Commission considers what actions universities in NSW can take in order to manage the corruption risks
sentences.section: Why the Commission produced this paper

sentences.text: Its research included university consultations, interviews with more than 40 academics and administrators, and review of relevant legislation and literature.
sentences.support: More than 40 academics and administrators with significant experience with international students were interviewed

sentences.text: The Commission identifies tensions between revenue generation and academic standards, alongside risks from market choices and reliance on recruitment agents.
sentences.support: This creates significant tensions within those universities between generation of revenue and compliance with academic standards.

sentences.text: The Commission highlights prevention approaches involving market risk assessment, closer oversight of agents and greater separation between recruitment and academic compliance.
sentences.support: separating the compliance function from the business development function, as feasible

findings.quote: This creates significant tensions within those universities between generation of revenue and compliance with academic standards.

notes: The introductory section Key corruption prevention initiatives summarises the report and its proposed approaches. There is no numbered formal recommendations list. Allegations of student or academic misconduct are not treated as established facts.
